proposals.before: At the beginning Dezong, having suffered many hardships, sought to indulge the frontier commands; whenever a commander died, he sent eunuchs to observe the army and see whom the masses wished to install — so great generals privately used gold and silks to court the inner court and seek a commission; in the late Yan years this was especially so, and regional picks did not come from the court.
proposals.after: At the beginning Dezong, having suffered many hardships, sought to indulge the frontier commands; whenever a commander died, he sent eunuchs to observe the army and see whom the masses wished to install — so great generals privately used gold and silks to court the inner court and seek a commission; in his late years this was especially so, and regional picks did not come from the court.
proposals.reason: 晏年 means late years of life or reign, not a Yan era; the literal line invents a Yan period.

proposals.before: He died the following year at seventy, was posthumously made Sikong, and given the temple name Xuanxian.
proposals.after: He died the following year at seventy, was posthumously made Situ, and given the posthumous title Xuanxian.
proposals.reason: 贈司徒 is Situ, not Sikong (司空), and 謚 is a posthumous title rather than a temple name.

proposals.before: The next year he died, age seventy; posthumously made Sikong, posthumous title Xuanxian.
proposals.after: The next year he died, age seventy; posthumously made Situ, posthumous title Xuanxian.
proposals.reason: The source writes 司徒 (Situ); Sikong would be 司空, already used as a different honorary office in the previous sentence.

proposals.before: After Xiao Ye's fall, eunuchs ruined him; Jiang Shen was chosen instead, Sheng was made honorary Minister of Rites and exiled to Tianping, where he died in frustration.
proposals.after: After Xiao Ye's fall, eunuchs ruined him; Jiang Shen was chosen instead, Sheng was made honorary Minister of Rites and sent out as military commissioner of Tianping, where he died in frustration.
proposals.reason: 出為天平節度使 is an outward regional posting, not exile; the literal English already renders it as a commissionership.

proposals.before: When Ji and historiographer Jiang Wu submitted Dezong's Veritable Record, Jifu argued that Ji, having left the history office on grounds of illness, should not present it, and had him made Grand Mentor while dismissing the historians.
proposals.after: When Ji and historiographer Jiang Wu submitted Dezong's Veritable Record, Jifu argued that Ji, having left the history office on grounds of illness, should not present it, and had him made Advisor to the Heir Apparent (太子賓客) while dismissing the historians.
proposals.reason: 太子賓客 is Advisor/Guest of the Heir Apparent, not Grand Mentor (太子太傅), which is the later posthumous honor in s0103.

proposals.before: Past forty years, distressed between Guangyang, he did not rouse himself; wife and children pursued blame — Fan was at ease as before.
proposals.after: Past forty years, distressed in Guangling, he did not rouse himself; wife and children pursued blame — Fan was at ease as before.
proposals.reason: 廣陵 is Guangling, not Guangyang.

proposals.before: When Jianfeng died, Haozhou prefect Du Jian hastily drove to arrive, secretly having a downward look; Fan wept and said: "You, sir, now in mourning — you ought carefully to guard the soil; why abandon and come?
proposals.after: When Jianfeng died, Haozhou prefect Du Jian hastily drove to arrive, secretly having ambitious designs; Fan wept and said: "The lord now has died — you, sir, ought carefully to guard your territory; why abandon it and come?
proposals.reason: 公今喪 refers to Zhang Jianfeng's death, not to Du Jian being in mourning.

proposals.before: They performed vulgar Yuzhou skits. Fan excused himself once and said, "I spend the day with you yet cannot understand a word!"
proposals.after: They performed comic skits and riddling talk. Fan excused himself after one visit and said, "I spend the day with you yet cannot understand a word!"
proposals.reason: 庾語 is enigmatic/riddling speech, not the place-name Yuzhou.

proposals.before: Zhongshu and others made comic skits with Yuzhou dialect mutually intimate; Fan on seeing once, apologized and did not go, saying: "I with you all day — I do not understand what language is spoken!
proposals.after: Zhongshu and others made comic skits and riddling talk in familiar jest; Fan on seeing them once apologized and did not go, saying: "I spend the whole day with you and do not understand what is being said!"
proposals.reason: 庾語 is riddling/enigmatic language, not Yuzhou dialect.

proposals.before: When Zheng Yin was dismissed, he was therefore appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Director.
proposals.after: When Zheng Yin was dismissed, he was therefore appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery (門下侍郎) and Associate Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
proposals.reason: 門下侍郎 belongs to the Chancellery, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: When Congshi sent Wang Yiyuan to court, Ji won him with calm persuasion until Yiyuan described Congshi's crimes ripe for action; Ji had already secured the loyalty of generals such as Wu Chongyin.
proposals.after: When Congshi sent Wang Yiyuan to court, Ji won him with calm persuasion until Yiyuan described Congshi's crimes as ripe for action; Ji had recently sent people over and obtained the key cooperation of Congshi's great generals such as Wu Chongyin.
proposals.reason: 比遣往，得其大將烏重胤等要領 describes a recent dispatch to obtain Wu Chongyin's essential points.

proposals.before: He died before taking post at fifty-eight, was posthumously made Vice Minister of Revenue, and given the temple name Zhenjian.
proposals.after: He died before taking post at fifty-eight, was posthumously made Minister of Revenue, and given the posthumous name Zhenjian.
proposals.reason: 戶部尚書 is Minister of Revenue, not Vice Minister; 謚 is a posthumous name, not a temple name.

proposals.before: Before departing he died, age fifty-eight; posthumously made Vice Minister of Revenue, posthumous title Zhenjian.
proposals.after: Before departing he died, age fifty-eight; posthumously made Minister of Revenue, posthumous title Zhenjian.
proposals.reason: 戶部尚書 is the minister, not the vice minister.

proposals.before: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Northern Zhou pillar of state Wei.
proposals.after: He was the eighth-generation descendant of Northern Zhou pillar of state Xiong.
proposals.reason: The ancestor's given name is 敻; English Wei drops that name.

proposals.before: Great-great-grandson eight generations removed of Zhou pillar of state Wei.
proposals.after: Eighth-generation descendant of the Later Zhou pillar of state Xiong.
proposals.reason: 八世孫 is eighth-generation descendant, not great-great-grandson.

proposals.before: He was later made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: He was later made Vice Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書少監 is a Palace Library post, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: After a long time, changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: After a long time, changed to Vice Director of the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書少監 is not a Secretariat office.

proposals.before: The next day Fan was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: The next day Fan was demoted to Chief of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is the heir's household administration, not Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: Su and others slandered him and, debating war before the emperor, had him demoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.after: Su and others slandered him; he also debated military affairs with Du before the emperor, and the discussion went largely against him, so he was demoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English omits 與度, Pei Du as debate counterpart.

proposals.before: He was demoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent at the eastern capital.
proposals.after: He was demoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, assigned to the eastern capital.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is the household supervisor of the heir apparent, not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: Zhou Chi of Zheng-Hua took him onto staff.
proposals.after: Zhou Chi, military commissioner of Zheng-Hua, memorialized to place him on his staff.
proposals.reason: 節度鄭滑 names Zhou Chi's posting, not a toponymic origin.

proposals.before: He died, was posthumously Vice Minister of Revenue, and styled Zhen.
proposals.after: He died, was posthumously made Minister of Revenue, and given the posthumous title Zhen.
proposals.reason: 戶部尚書 is Minister of Revenue, not Vice Minister.

proposals.before: When Dengzhou prefect Xue Hongzong was dismissed, the emperor's admonition drawn from the book astonished every official.
proposals.after: When Dengzhou prefect Xue Hongzong attended the thanksgiving audience, the emperor's admonition on prefectural affairs astonished every official.
proposals.reason: 中謝 is the ritual audience of thanks after appointment, not dismissal.

proposals.before: In Taihe 5 the ancestral temple leaked; Wenzong, angry at delay, stripped officials and ordered eunuchs to repair.
proposals.after: In Taihe 5 the ancestral temple leaked; Wenzong, angry at delay, blamed Director Li Rui and Supervisor Wang Kan, stripped their salaries, and ordered eunuchs to repair.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops named officials present in the Chinese and literal lines.

proposals.before: At first, Wen concurrently served as lecturer-reader to Crown Prince Zhuangyi. In the morning he went to the palace; at midday he saw the Crown Prince and remonstrated: "Your Highness is in flourishing years. You should rise at cockcrow and ask after the Son of Heaven's well-being, following King Wen's precedent."
proposals.after: At first, Wen concurrently served as lecturer-reader to Crown Prince Zhuangke. In the morning he went to the palace; at midday he saw the Crown Prince and remonstrated: "Your Highness is in flourishing years. You should rise at cockcrow and ask after the Son of Heaven's well-being, following King Wen's precedent."
proposals.reason: The posthumous title uses ke, not yi, for the character in the Chinese name.

proposals.before: Wang Yanping left Lingwu with horses and armor, bribed his way from Kangzhou registrar to Fuzhou marshal; musician Yuchi Zhang was made Guangzhou chief administrator — Wen sealed and returned all such edicts.
proposals.after: Wang Yanping left Lingwu with horses and armor, bribed his way from Kangzhou registrar to Fuzhou marshal; musician Yuchi Zhang was made Guang prefecture chief administrator — Wen sealed and returned all such edicts.
proposals.reason: The place name is Guang prefecture, not Guangzhou.

proposals.before: At the time many straightened his words.
proposals.after: At the time many regarded his words as upright.
proposals.reason: The phrase means contemporaries judged the speech frank and correct.

proposals.before: Yao Xu, an investigating official of the Salt and Iron Monopoly, handled major cases; the emperor considered him able and promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Appointments, Outer Section. As he was about to hurry to the ministry, Wen sent a household member to stop him and immediately memorialized: "The pure selection of gentlemen-officials cannot be used to reward capable clerks."
proposals.after: Yao Xu, an investigating official of the Salt and Iron Monopoly, handled major cases; the emperor considered him able and promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Operations, Outer Section. As he was about to hurry to the ministry, Wen sent a household member to stop him and immediately memorialized: "The pure selection of gentlemen-officials cannot be used to reward capable clerks."
proposals.reason: The office is the Bureau of Operations, not Appointments.

proposals.before: Female craft adept at literature — continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women — circulated in the world.
proposals.after: She was skilled at literature — continued Lady Cao's Admonitions for Women — circulated in the world.
proposals.reason: The subject is the daughter as writer, not needlework as a craft label.

decisions.reason: 晏年 means Dezong's late years, not a Yan era; the original invents a period name.
贈司徒 is a posthumous Situ, distinct from 司空 in the previous sentence, and 謚 is a posthumous title, not a temple name.
The source grants 司徒, not 司空; Sikong is the honorary office already named in the preceding sentence.
出為天平節度使 is an outward posting as military commissioner, not exile.

decisions.after: When Ji and historiographer Jiang Wu submitted Dezong's Veritable Record, Jifu argued that Ji, having left the history office on grounds of illness, should not present it, and had him made Advisor to the Heir Apparent while dismissing the historians.
decisions.reason: 太子賓客 is Advisor to the Heir Apparent, not Grand Mentor (the later 太子太傅). The proposed Chinese gloss is accurate but awkward in idiomatic English.
廣陵 is Guangling; Guangyang is a wrong place-name, and 間 here is not “between.”
公今喪 refers to Jianfeng's death; 君 is Du Jian, who is told to keep his own territory, while 陰有顗望 marks ambitious designs, not a downward look.
庾語 is riddling, enigmatic speech, not the toponym Yuzhou; 俳說 is comic jesting.
庾語 is riddling talk, not a Yuzhou dialect; 相狎昵 is familiar jest, and Fan declined after one visit.

decisions.after: When Zheng Yin was dismissed, he was therefore appointed Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Associate Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
decisions.reason: 門下侍郎 is a Chancellery vice-ministership, not a Secretariat post, but the proposed English embeds Chinese characters and must be given in English only.

decisions.reason: 比遣往 is a recent dispatch, not a prior fait accompli, and 要領 is the essential hold on Congshi's generals, not loyalty already secured.

尚書 is the ministerial rank; vice minister would be 侍郎.
The ancestor named in the source is 敻 (Xiong); rendering that given name as Wei drops the name the text actually supplies.
八世孫 is an eighth-generation descendant, not a great-great-grandson, and the named ancestor is 敻 of the Later Zhou.
秘書少監 belongs to the Palace Library (秘書省), not the Secretariat.
秘書少監 is not a Secretariat office.
太子詹事 is the heir's household administration, not Grand Mentor (太傅).
The original omits 與度 as debate counterpart and compresses 議頗駁, which records that the discussion went against Guanzhi.

decisions.reason: 太子詹事 is the heir's household supervisor, not Grand Mentor, and 分司東都 is an eastern-capital assignment.

decisions.reason: 節度鄭滑 names Zhou Chi's military commission, not his native place, and 表署幕府 is a memorialized staff appointment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 周墀節度鄭滑，表署幕府

decisions.reason: 戶部尚書 is Minister of Revenue, not vice minister, and 謚曰貞 is a posthumous title.
中謝 is the thanksgiving audience after appointment, not dismissal, and 敕戒州事 is an admonition on prefectural affairs.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 薛弘宗中謝，帝敕戒州事

decisions.reason: The source names Director Li Rui and Supervisor Wang Kan and records that their salaries were stripped, which the original English omits.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 責卿李銳、監王堪，奪其稟

decisions.reason: 莊恪 is Zhuangke; 恪 is ke, not the yi of 懿.
光州 is Guang Prefecture, not 廣州 (Guangzhou).
直其言 means contemporaries judged the speech upright, not that they straightened the wording.
職方員外郎 is the Bureau of Operations, not Appointments.
女工屬文 takes the daughter as subject skilled at composing, not “female craft” as needlework.
